title: Prefetch fingerprinting and granular swap controller for paged KV cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency and unnecessary GPU-host swap I/O by making prefetch decisions per-request using a lightweight fingerprint of token ancestry and batch dynamics, plus a granular swap controller that applies hysteresis and token-affinity heuristics.
background: We currently use size- and recency-driven eviction for the paged/blocked KV slab allocator. That causes two inefficiencies: (1) bulk prefetching of large KV regions for requests that only touch a small prefix, and (2) reactive host->GPU swap storms when multiple concurrent requests evict overlapping working sets. Previous experiments (ENG-214999, ENG-220456) improved scheduling but left per-request signalization limited to coarse hotset metrics.
proposal: 1) Compute a 64-bit fingerprint per request derived from: model version, prompt hash (prefix), token position distribution, and a small signature of recent cache hits. Use this fingerprint to map the request to a preferred KV slice affinity.
proposal_2: 2) Prefetch policy: translate fingerprint -> ordered list of candidate slab segments (top-3) to prefetch. Prefetch budget is bounded by request latency SLA and batch size. For streaming requests, perform incremental prefetch only for predicted next segments.
proposal_3: 3) Granular swap controller: instead of evicting whole slabs eagerly, apply sliding hysteresis based on segment access frequency and recent prefetch miss-rate. If evictions are needed, demote to host staging with a 'soft-reserve' keep-window for segments that have high token-affinity scores.
implementation_notes:
- Fingerprinting is implemented as a deterministic xor/rotate mix of canonical IDs to keep compute < 200ns per request.
- Prefetch selector is pure read-only map indexed by (model, fingerprint prefix) and can be updated with live telemetry.
- Swap controller hooks into allocator's free path and consults the live hotset estimator; includes counters for demote/restore churn.
- Add a lightweight per-segment telemetry tag to measure restore latency and host I/O bytes.
perf_targets:
- Reduce 99p KV restore latency by 35% on mixed short/long prompt workloads.
- Reduce host-to-GPU read bandwidth for cold tails by 30% under 80% GPU residency.
- Keep median generation latency within existing SLA (+5ms tolerance for prefetch accounting).
safety_and_fallback: If prefetching increases observed latency on a given route for 3 successive cycles, automatically disable fingerprint-based prefetch for that route and fall back to recency-driven batching. Swap controller has a conservative fail-open: if memory pressure is detected across the pool, it falls back to current global eviction policy.
observability: Expose metrics: fingerprint_hit_rate, prefetch_bandwidth_by_route, segment_restore_latency_histogram, swap_demote_churn, prefetch_backpressure_count. Add log lines for suppressed prefetch decisions and early abort reasons. Wire trace spans for prefetch and restore operations.
api_and_config: New runtime flags (configurable per-customer/route): prefetch.enabled (bool), prefetch.budget_ms (int), prefetch.top_k (int), swap_controller.hysteresis_ms (int), swap_controller.soft_reserve_ratio (float). Defaults chosen conservatively for hosted tenants.
open_questions:
- How often should the fingerprint->segment mapping be recomputed from telemetry? (epoch vs sliding window).
- Should we allow customers to opt out of fingerprinting for privacy-sensitive prefixes? (prefix hashing vs salted hashing).
- Interaction with quantized model variants: does a fingerprint derived from architecture need to include quantization profile?

- Prefetch selector PoC + perf harness (in progress).

- Canary rollout to 5% of runtime requests with extended telemetry (planned).
